title: Token-aware GPU batch scheduling
subtitle: The token is the unit of GPU scheduling in my broker: shape-pure batches packed to each card's declared limits, across two different GPUs.

stats.label: key-value cache hit rate on both cards, zero shape switches
lanes in use at 22 percent lane pressure
lane reuses a second, one new lane every two seconds

lede: Inference Fabric started from a backlog of billions of tokens and two GPUs of different sizes. A queue that hands each card whatever arrived next mixes short and long prompts, fills the gaps with padding, thrashes the engine's key-value cache and sends the smaller card work it cannot hold. I made the token the broker's unit of scheduling and split the problem into two separate axes: a signature for cacheable structure and lanes for length. Shape is declared by the producer, which knows its own prompt template. Each cacheable component of a prompt is hashed and appended in order, and the list is reduced to one 64-bit signature. The broker never parses a prompt and never sees the model.
quote: The rule I wrote at the top of that code: spend structure before spending waste.
evidence: Token-aware scheduling: a Rust broker that packs shape-pure batches to each GPU's declared limits, at 0.421% padding waste across both cards.
KV-cache-aware batching: a 64-bit shape signature per prompt template held a 99.9% key-value cache hit rate on both cards with zero shape switches.
Message broker and queue design: rolling lanes with a pressure-adaptive threshold, 2,280 lanes in use at 22 percent lane pressure and ≈17,800 lane reuses a second.
author: Corey James
